mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 declines by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four consecutive months of INDPRO decline.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in FEDFUNDS and a decline in CPIAUCSL above 0.5% month-over-month indicates a restrictive monetary policy stance with falling inflation, which historically coincides with equity market pullbacks over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls by >0.5% month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls by more than 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and real retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and RSAFS both exceed 12-month moving averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and RSAFS exceed their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which raises wage pressures and input costs, ultimately leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to margin compression.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE remains below 4% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE remains below 4% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader market gains over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST exceeds 12-month moving average for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during six consecutive months where HOUST exceeds its 12-month moving average.
